method.auditData: raw samplesMs and per-round subject order are retained by default; --no-samples is an explicit local-only size optimization

excludedSubjects.@kxsystems/*: KX publishes no Node.js q client on npm

method.memory: process-wide RSS/heap delta around retained decoded results with forced GC at both snapshots; a noisy diagnostic, not a library footprint
method.payloadBytes: server-side `count -8!table` for the fixture table: a logical payload size shared by all subjects, not observed wire bytes
method.readComparability: every subject decodes an identical server byte stream into its documented representation, so all are ranked; timed validation proves the decoded row count, not table content fidelity. Exact int64 and nanosecond atom probes are recorded in `fidelity`; `roundTripStates` separately distinguishes identical, differs, resized, and unverified decode-then-encode outcomes without assigning an encoder failure to the decoder
method.scalarComparability: value-exact latency floor; a subject that cannot return the exact value is listed in `unsupported` instead of being ranked
method.scheduling: one request in flight per subject; every round runs each subject once in a deterministic order reshuffled from `orderSeed`, so positions and predecessors both vary; a cyclic rotation would pin every subject behind the same neighbour in every round
method.sendComparability: sends are compared only for subjects whose decoded value re-encodes to a q-identical value of the same canonical size; others are listed in `unsupported` with no samples, throughput, or ratio
method.throughput: payloadBytes divided by the median duration
method.untimedCorrectnessChecks: int64 and nanosecond-timestamp exactness are reported by the preflight, not timed: timing a wrong decode against a right one would compare different work

notes: sub-millisecond timestamps need includeNanosecond:true, measured here on a second connection; in that mode temporal values become text and the encoder rejects them, so tables cannot be sent back
int64 decodes to double and loses precision beyond 2^53; timestamps decode to millisecond Date
long2number:false and nanos2date:false restore exactness with Long wrappers but roughly double decode time
